long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Florenceville, New Brunswick, within the family that created McCain Foods, Michael H. McCain entered the food business early in his career. He worked across its Canadian and United States operations, eventually leading McCain Foods USA. He joined Maple Leaf Foods in 1995 and became chief executive three years later.

Over the next 25 years, McCain refocused Maple Leaf around packaged protein and advanced a sustainability programme that included carbon neutrality. He also drove the creation of the Maple Leaf Centre for Food Security. After transferring the chief executive role to Curtis Frank in 2023, McCain remained executive chair while retaining control through McCain Capital. He became executive chair of Canada Packers when it separated from Maple Leaf two years later.

confidence.reason: The two-paragraph career arc is supported by Maple Leaf's current biography, management circular, 2025 separation announcement and integrated report. It separates the inherited family context from McCain's own operating record and current stewardship.
